Jonas — legal review below and attached redline. High level positions we should take:

1) Roles and definitions
- Controller: Acme Corp. Processor: Redwood Inference.
- Embeddings: treat as "derived outputs" produced by processing customer-provided inputs. If embeddings are reversible to PII (per Acme's risk assessment), treat operationally as Processed Personal Data subject to controller instructions. We propose a narrow definition to preserve model outputs but allow deletion on request.

2) Logs / telemetry
- Categories: request payloads (full text), system traces (internal stack/metrics), aggregated anonymized telemetry.
- Retention: propose 30 days for full request payloads; 180 days for aggregated, non-identifiable metrics. If Acme requires 90 days for request payloads, counter with 60 days as a compromise.
- Pseudonymization: we will hash identifiers and rotate keys; include example language for pseudonymization in Section 4.2.

3) Subprocessors
- Current list attached (subprocessors-list.csv). We notify customers 30 days prior to onboarding any new subprocessor and maintain a published list. We cannot accept unlimited prior approval; our standard is 30-day notice with right to object.

4) Transfers / hosting
- Primary transfer mechanism: EU SCCs (2021/2022 versions depending on region).
- EU-only hosting: available as a Dedicated or Private deployment addendum (fee-based). Add an exhibit allowing customer to require EU-only processing and storage; execution of the addendum will enforce region-specific data residency.

5) Deletion / embeddings
- On data deletion request, we will remove customer-provided inputs and purge embeddings from hot caches within 48 hours; longer-living backups may be addressed in Exhibit B. Propose explicit deletion SLA language.

I've added inline edits to the attached Redwood_DPA_redlines_v1.docx. I also included the current subprocessors CSV. Recommend we send this package to Acme with a suggested DocuSign envelope and 7 business day turnaround.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
